baseline.name: Build a new list of unique sorted values
baseline.approach: Scan the original list and allocate one new node per distinct value.
baseline.space: O(u) newly allocated output nodes for u distinct values; O(1) other state

archived.name: Unlink and free duplicate nodes
archived.time: O(n), where n is the number of list nodes
archived.space: O(1) auxiliary space; list links are modified and removed nodes are freed

why: Reusing the existing unique nodes avoids building an independent output list.
quantitative_comparison: Both inspect a linear number of links. The copy baseline allocates u output nodes; the archived source allocates no new nodes and frees n-u duplicates. This compares allocation volume, not elapsed time or universal memory safety.
tradeoffs: Requires ownership compatible with freeing removed nodes and invalidates aliases to them. A copied output preserves the original list and its node identities.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
